name: Robotic Pool Cleaner
definition: A self-propelled pool-cleaning machine that operates underwater and uses onboard or tethered power, drive, debris collection and filtration to clean manufacturer-declared pool surfaces.
includedScope: Corded and cordless submerged robotic pool cleaners
Models documented for pool floor, wall or waterline cleaning
excludedScope: Suction-side and pressure-side cleaners without onboard propulsion
Surface-only skimmers and household floor robots
primaryApplications: Residential in-ground and above-ground pool cleaning within declared limits
Pool floor, wall and waterline debris collection where model-approved
headline: Robotic pool cleaner drive, filters, coverage and buyer checks
description: This profile separates corded and cordless power, underwater drive, navigation, brushes, debris filters, cleaning cycles, pool geometry, retrieval, charging and connectivity so buyers can verify the actual pool-model fit.
metaDescription: Robotic pool cleaner guide covering corded and cordless types, coverage, filters, models, safety and buyer checks.
disclaimer: This independent category reference is not pool-safety, electrical, water-chemistry or diving advice. Confirm the exact regional model, manual, pool dimensions, shape, surface, depth, chemistry, power supply or charger, filter, cable, retrieval and bather-exclusion procedure.

keyFacts.label: Category boundary
keyFacts.value: Self-propelled underwater machine with onboard debris filtration
keyFacts.evidence: Official product pages describe powered drive, brushing, suction flow and removable filters.
keyFacts.scope: Named submerged pool robots; surface skimmers excluded.

keyFacts.label: Buyer verification
keyFacts.value: Match pool geometry, surface, depth, size, chemistry and retrieval to exact model
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturers publish materially different pool and coverage limits.

systemFlow.name: Power and control
systemFlow.componentFamily: Tethered supply or battery, controller, charger and communications
systemFlow.role: Supplies and controls underwater drive, pump and cleaning cycle.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources distinguish corded and cordless architectures.
systemFlow.scope: Exact supply, charger, firmware and market.

systemFlow.name: Mobility and cleaning
systemFlow.componentFamily: Tracks or wheels, navigation sensors, brushes, pump, inlet and filter basket
systemFlow.role: Moves across approved surfaces, agitates debris and filters water through onboard collection.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturers publish model-specific coverage and filtration systems.
systemFlow.scope: Declared pool geometry and surfaces only.

variants.name: Corded robotic pool cleaner
variants.taskScale: Scheduled pool floor, wall or waterline cycles
variants.operatorRelationship: User positions a low-voltage supply and manages a floating cable
variants.spaceConstraints: Outlet, supply clearance, cable length, pool geometry and storage
variants.limitations: Cable length does not establish effective coverage or anti-tangle performance.
variants.evidence: Maytronics and Aquabot publish corded robot configurations.
variants.scope: Exact cable, power supply and pool.

variants.name: Cordless robotic pool cleaner
variants.operatorRelationship: User charges, deploys, retrieves and rinses the robot and filter
variants.spaceConstraints: Charging location, carried mass, runtime, retrieval and storage
variants.limitations: Maximum runtime or area does not guarantee full coverage.
variants.evidence: Beatbot, Aiper, Polaris and WYBOT publish cordless models.

performanceMetrics.name: Cleaning coverage
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Which pool zones a model is designed to traverse and clean
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Floor, wall, waterline, surface, steps and platforms must be stated separately
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: An area limit does not prove navigation of every shape or obstacle.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official pages publish different zone and pool-shape boundaries.
performanceMetrics.scope: Exact model, mode, surface and pool geometry.

performanceMetrics.name: Cycle, runtime and filtration
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Available cleaning time and declared debris-capture architecture
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Mode, battery state, pump load, filter state, water and debris differ
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: GPH, microns or maximum runtime alone do not establish cleaning result.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Manufacturers publish model-specific cycles, runtime and filters.

applicationFit.application: In-ground pool floor, walls and waterline
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Run complete observed cycles in the actual pool and map missed zones, stalls and retrieval.
applicationFit.basis: Shape, slope, surface, obstacles, water depth, traction and navigation interact.
applicationFit.limitations: No universal wall, step or waterline coverage is implied.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Record cycle, zones, debris, stalls, cable or battery state and retrieval effort.
applicationFit.evidence: Official pages declare exact-model coverage and pool limits.

applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Verify slope, liner, size and floor-only boundary before trial.
applicationFit.basis: Some entry models exclude walls and restrict bottom slope.
applicationFit.limitations: Pool-type wording does not override the detailed manual.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Measure pool, confirm liner approval and observe edge parking and retrieval.
applicationFit.evidence: WYBOT publishes explicit floor-only and slope limits for A1.
applicationFit.scope: Named model and declared pool boundary.

componentStack.name: Power, drive and navigation
componentStack.role: Powers underwater movement and determines the cleaning path.
componentStack.evidence: Official sources document distinct power and navigation systems.
componentStack.scope: No cross-model charger, battery or cable fit.

componentStack.name: Brush, flow and filter
componentStack.role: Agitates approved surfaces and captures debris in the onboard basket or panels.
componentStack.evidence: Manufacturers publish different brush and filter architectures.

distinguishingSpecifications: Floor, wall, waterline and surface coverage
representativeModels.evidence: Beatbot publishes the named coverage, charging and filtration.
representativeModels.scope: Current US model and stated modes.

representativeModels.evidence: Aiper publishes the named product configuration.
Polaris publishes the product and manual.
WYBOT publishes the named model and qualifications.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Actual-zone coverage, stalls, filtration and retrieval
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Ranking by maximum area, runtime, GPH or sensor count
procurementDecisions.assessment: Run multiple observed full cycles in the intended pool.
procurementDecisions.basis: Pool geometry, surface, water, debris, navigation and traction interact.
procurementDecisions.limitations: No catalogue metric guarantees complete coverage.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Map missed areas and record debris, stalls, cycle time and handling.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources show different pool and mode boundaries.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Battery or supply, cable, filter, brush, app and service parts
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Assuming family labels or visual fit establish compatibility
procurementDecisions.assessment: Attach exact part codes and retrieval procedure to the quote.
procurementDecisions.basis: Critical assemblies and firmware are model-specific.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Future cloud or part availability is not guaranteed.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Obtain part numbers, service terms, update policy and manual procedure.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Product pages and manuals identify exact systems.

engineeringChecks.reason: Powered equipment, chargers and supplies require strict separation from swimmers and water per instructions.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Follow the exact manual for deployment, power-supply placement, charging and removal before bathing.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official manuals define operating and safety procedures.
engineeringChecks.scope: Exact product and local electrical rules.

engineeringChecks.reason: Traction, materials, seals, weight and water release affect coverage and handling.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Confirm surface, salt/chlorine limits, depth, dry weight and retrieval method in writing.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manufacturers declare different pool and handling boundaries.

standards.name: Manufacturer model manual and regional conformity declaration
standards.applicability: Primary operational, electrical, charging, bather-exclusion and pool-compatibility requirements for the exact robot.
standards.evidence: Maytronics and Polaris publish model manuals; one Maytronics manual states applicable EU directives.
standards.scope: Exact model and market; no universal pool-robot standard claim is made.

developments.title: Polaris demonstrated FREEDOM Plus cordless retrieval control
developments.summary: Polaris published an official product presentation describing underwater remote control and waterline retrieval.
developments.evidence: The official Polaris product and video materials document the functionality.
